questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Seldom a government has faced such widespread public opposition.
Seldom has a government faced such widespread public opposition.
Seldom does a government faced such widespread public opposition.
Seldom a government faces such widespread public opposition has.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials like 'seldom' at the start trigger inversion: 'Seldom has a government faced...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It is imperative that the minister resigns immediately.
It is imperative that the minister resign immediately.
It is imperative that the minister will resign immediately.
It is imperative that the minister resigning immediately.
questions.explanation: After 'it is imperative that', formal English uses the subjunctive (base form): 'the minister resign immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Were it not for the opposition's protests, the bill would have passed unchallenged.
Were it not the opposition's protests, the bill would have passed unchallenged.
Was it not for the opposition's protests, the bill would have passed unchallenged.
Were it not for the opposition's protests, the bill will have passed unchallenged.
questions.explanation: 'Were it not for' is a formal inverted conditional meaning 'if it weren't for': 'Were it not for the protests, the bill would have passed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The coalition survived the vote, albeit with a much reduced majority.
The coalition survived the vote, albeit that a much reduced majority.
The coalition survived the vote, albeit it a much reduced majority.
The coalition survived the vote albeit for a much reduced majority.
questions.explanation: 'Albeit' introduces a concession and is typically followed directly by a prepositional or noun phrase: 'albeit with a reduced majority.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It was the opposition leader who first raised the corruption allegations.
It was the opposition leader which first raised the corruption allegations.
It was the opposition leader whom first raised the corruption allegations.
It the opposition leader was who first raised the corruption allegations.
questions.explanation: Cleft sentences for emphasis on a person use 'It was [person] who...': 'It was the opposition leader who first raised...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The senator asserts that the policy will reduce unemployment.
The senator asserts to that the policy will reduce unemployment.
The senator asserts the policy will reducing unemployment.
The senator is assert that the policy will reduce unemployment.
questions.explanation: 'Assert' (formal reporting verb) is followed by 'that + clause': 'asserts that the policy will reduce unemployment.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Having reviewed the evidence, the committee recommended further investigation.
Having review the evidence, the committee recommended further investigation.
Have reviewed the evidence, the committee recommended further investigation.
Having reviewed the evidence, the committee recommending further investigation.
questions.explanation: 'Having + past participle' shows a completed action before the main clause: 'Having reviewed the evidence, the committee recommended...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The vast majority of voters has expressed dissatisfaction with the current administration.
The vast majority of voters have expressed dissatisfaction with the current administration.
A vast majority of voters is expressed dissatisfaction with the current administration.
The vast majority of voters express dissatisfaction with the current administration already.
questions.explanation: 'The majority of' + plural noun typically takes a plural verb: 'the vast majority of voters have expressed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The government needn't have imposed such strict measures; the situation improved on its own.
The government needn't imposed such strict measures; the situation improved on its own.
The government didn't need have imposed such strict measures; the situation improved on its own.
The government needn't have impose such strict measures; the situation improved on its own.
questions.explanation: 'Needn't have + past participle' expresses an unnecessary past action: 'needn't have imposed such strict measures.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Not only did the reform pass, but public approval also rose.
Not only the reform passed, but public approval also rose.
Not only did the reform pass, but also public approval rose.
Not only the reform did pass, but public approval also rose.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' at the start of a clause triggers inversion: 'Not only did the reform pass, but public approval also rose.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is arguably the most controversial policy of the decade.
This is arguable the most controversial policy of the decade.
This arguably is the most controversial policy of the decade it.
This is arguably that the most controversial policy of the decade.
questions.explanation: 'Arguably' is an adverb used to hedge a strong claim: 'this is arguably the most controversial policy.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The government introduced a system whereby citizens can report corruption anonymously.
The government introduced a system where citizens can report corruption anonymously by.
The government introduced a system by which whereby citizens can report corruption.
The government introduced a system whereby that citizens can report corruption anonymously.
questions.explanation: 'Whereby' means 'by which' and introduces a formal relative clause describing a process: 'a system whereby citizens can report corruption.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: So fierce was the debate that the session was adjourned early.
So fierce the debate was that the session was adjourned early.
So fierce was the debate the session was adjourned early.
So fierce was that the debate the session was adjourned early.
questions.explanation: Fronting 'so + adjective' for emphasis triggers inversion: 'So fierce was the debate that the session was adjourned.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The ratification of the treaty marked a turning point in foreign policy.
The ratify of the treaty marked a turning point in foreign policy.
The ratification of the treaty mark a turning point in foreign policy.
The ratifying the treaty marked a turning point in foreign policy.
questions.explanation: Formal writing nominalizes verbs: 'ratify' becomes 'the ratification of...'

questions.topic: Passive with modal perfect (could have been)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The crisis could have been averted if officials had responded promptly.
The crisis could been averted if officials had responded promptly.
The crisis could have averted if officials had responded promptly.
The crisis could have being averted if officials had responded promptly.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + past participle: 'could have been averted.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some officials favor sanctions; others, diplomacy.
Some officials favor sanctions; others favor, diplomacy.
Some officials favor sanctions; others is diplomacy.
Some officials favor sanctions; others favors diplomacy.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits the repeated verb after a semicolon: 'others, diplomacy' (= others favor diplomacy).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The proposal faced strong criticism. Nevertheless, it was approved.
The proposal faced strong criticism, nevertheless it was approved.
The proposal faced strong criticism. Nevertheless it was approved.
The proposal faced strong criticism nevertheless, it was approved.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The proposal faced criticism. Nevertheless, it was approved.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Notwithstanding the criticism, the president signed the bill into law.
Notwithstanding of the criticism, the president signed the bill into law.
Notwithstanding the criticism, but the president signed the bill into law.
The criticism notwithstanding of, the president signed the bill into law.
questions.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' is a formal preposition meaning 'despite' and is followed directly by a noun phrase: 'Notwithstanding the criticism...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting a meeting with a local official?
options: I'm writing to see if you wanna meet up sometime.
I am writing to request a meeting at your earliest convenience to discuss community concerns.
Hey, can we meet? I have some concerns.
Just wondering if you're free to chat about the neighborhood.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to request a meeting at your earliest convenience...' is a standard formal opening for official correspondence.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a delayed public service?
options: I'm super annoyed that the service is so delayed.
I am writing to draw your attention to the persistent delays in the delivery of this public service.
The service is delayed, and I want to complain.
I am writing to draw your attention to the persistent delays in the delivery of this public service, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use precise, measured language such as 'I am writing to draw your attention to...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The two parties met to iron out their differences before the vote.
The two parties met to iron their differences out before the vote of.
The two parties met to iron the differences of before the vote out.
The two parties met to iron out of their differences before the vote.
questions.explanation: 'Iron out' means 'to resolve' and is commonly used with 'differences': 'iron out their differences before the vote.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The bill got rejected by the senate after a heated debate.
The bill got reject by the senate after a heated debate.
The bill got rejecting by the senate after a heated debate.
The bill was got rejected by the senate after a heated debate.
questions.explanation: Informal/semi-formal passive with 'get': get + past participle: 'the bill got rejected by the senate.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: All things considered, the reform was a reasonable compromise.
All things consider, the reform was a reasonable compromise.
All things considering, the reform was a reasonable compromise.
All things considered that, the reform was a reasonable compromise.
questions.explanation: 'All things considered' is a fixed absolute participle phrase meaning 'taking everything into account.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In light of the recent scandal, the minister resigned.
In the light of the recent scandal, the minister resigned, that.
Light of the recent scandal, the minister resigned.
In light for the recent scandal, the minister resigned.
questions.explanation: 'In light of' means 'considering' and is followed by a noun phrase: 'In light of the recent scandal...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The proposed reform drew sharp criticism from opposition parties.
The proposed reform made sharp criticism draw from opposition parties.
The proposed reform gave sharp criticism draw from opposition parties.
The proposed reform drew of sharp criticism from opposition parties.
questions.explanation: 'Draw criticism' is a fixed collocation meaning 'to attract criticism': 'the reform drew sharp criticism.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The administration has consistently denied any wrongdoing.
The administration has denied consistently any wrongdoing.
Consistently the administration has denied any wrongdoing.
The administration consistently has denied any wrongdoing.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency in formal writing typically follow the auxiliary verb: 'has consistently denied.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The policy lacks clear funding. Furthermore, its timeline is unrealistic.
The policy lacks clear funding, furthermore its timeline is unrealistic.
The policy lacks clear funding. Furthermore its timeline is unrealistic.
The policy lacks clear funding furthermore, its timeline is unrealistic.
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The policy lacks funding. Furthermore, its timeline is unrealistic.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: The senator would seldom compromise on this issue, would he?
The senator would seldom compromise on this issue, wouldn't he?
The senator would seldom compromise on this issue, don't he?
The senator would seldom compromise on this issue, does he?
questions.explanation: 'Seldom' makes the statement effectively negative, so the tag is positive: 'would seldom compromise..., would he?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The negotiations were not entirely successful.
The negotiations were not all successful entirely.
The negotiations not were entirely successful.
The negotiations were entirely not successful.
questions.explanation: Formal understatement places 'not' before the adverb: 'The negotiations were not entirely successful.'

questions.topic: Advanced conditionals (Had it not been for)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Had it not been for international pressure, the ceasefire would have collapsed.
Had it not for international pressure, the ceasefire would have collapsed.
Had it not been international pressure, the ceasefire would have collapsed.
Had it not been for international pressure, the ceasefire will have collapsed.
questions.explanation: 'Had it not been for' is a formal inverted past conditional meaning 'if it hadn't been for': 'Had it not been for the pressure, the ceasefire would have collapsed.'
